attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He cites Sutskever as agreeing but makes the claim in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'apparently' for the diminishing-returns part, so the hedge survives. It rightly leaves out the separate claim about hallucination, generalisation, planning and reasoning. It is an observation, but the hedged core is not scorable.

contract.note: Fair. 'Appear' is an epistemic hedge, and Marcus named no measure, denominator or set of models. Treating the trend as a definite decline would overstate what he committed to.

reviews.rationale: The core of the claim, diminishing returns from scaling, is hedged as an appearance and names no metric, so policy does not allow it to be scored. The 'measurable improvements' part is weak, and it does not make the hedged trend a firm claim. The packet has no evidence items and lists no counterevidence. The outcome is not_adjudicable.
